I completed an online triage earlier in the week regarding sinus symptoms. By Friday my condition had worsened significantly, including loss of hearing, blurred vision and vertigo, so I contacted the practice.

The receptionist, Jo, told me my request had been reviewed and was “not urgent” and that I would be booked an appointment within five days. I explained multiple times that my symptoms had developed and worsened, and that I needed help completing a new triage as I could not access the online system due to blurred vision. She refused to assist, repeatedly spoke over me, and ultimately terminated the call.

Reception staff are not clinicians and should not be deciding urgency or blocking access to care. Their role is to listen, document symptoms, and escalate appropriately. This did not happen.

I later spoke to another member of staff who involved the duty GP, and I was seen within the hour. Had I not pushed for help, I would likely have ended up in A&E.
